newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish PM Bruton signals he plans a June election.
newsitem.headline: Irish PM Bruton signals he plans a June election.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton signalled on Sunday he is likely to call a June general election within days.
Bruton, who heads a three-party coalition, told Irish radio he was looking at an election next month and hoped a new parliament would be in session by the end of June.

The Fine Gael party leader hopes voters will again back his centre-left "Rainbow Coalition" with the Labour Party and Democratic Left against a possible centre-right challenge from Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democratic Party.
But a newspaper opinion poll showed Fianna Fail had increased its standing by five percent to 45 percent since a similar poll two months ago.
"Good news for Fianna Fail, bad news for everybody else" was how the Sunday Tribune newspaper summed up the results of the poll carried out by Lansdowne Markets Surveys.
Fine Gael had slipped by two points to 26 percent while Labour and Democratic Left were each down by one point to 11 percent and one percent respectively.
Fifteen percent of voters were undecided, the poll showed.

"With the general election campaign due to begin this week, Fianna Fail is now in a good position to win the extra seats needed to put the party back into government, according to the (poll) results," wrote Sunday Tribune political correspondent Stephen Collins.
The Progressive Democratic Party had dropped two points and unless it improved on its six percent standing, "it may not have the numbers needed to form a Fianna Fail-PD government", Collins said.
